**Measured this fire — the write-side half of this card is disproven. Evidence only; ⛔ no grading, no label change (skills lane self-triages).**

This card's read-side claim is confirmed, and its explicitly-inferred write-side claim ("a seat that appends a line by rewriting a card body may store `'` literals into its code blocks") **does not reproduce**. The escaping is a **read-path rendering artifact only**.

**The experiment**, run on #8811 with the pre-write body held for rollback:

1. Read #8811's body via MCP — apostrophes/quotes come back as `'` / `"`, as this card describes.
2. Wrote the body back with those entities **decoded to literal `'` and `"`**, plus a `Blocked-by:` first line.
3. Read it back: entities render as `'` / `"` — **identical to step 1, not `&#39;`**. No double-encoding, no corruption of the fenced/inline code. Repeated on #8810 with the same result, including a markdown blockquote (`>`) round-tripping intact.

**So the correct procedure is: decode entities before writing back.** A seat that echoes the *escaped* read straight back is the case that would corrupt — which is the real hazard, and the opposite of "don't touch bodies".

⚠️ **One genuine finding the experiment turned up, which is not what this card predicted:** an HTML comment (`<!-- ... -->`) placed in the body was **silently stripped** by the sanitizer, leaving blank lines. So bodies do lose content on write — just not via entity mangling. Anything a seat needs to survive must be visible markdown, never an HTML comment.

**Why this is worth more than the card itself.** The unmeasured fear here has been load-bearing: it is the stated reason `Blocked-by:` lines have been going into comments instead of bodies, and the 2026-08-14 sweep found **26 of 40 open `pm:blocked` cards across the three repos carry no body-level line** — meaning the reverse index the unlock scan greps is missing on roughly two-thirds of blocked cards. That channel defect has been recorded six times without being settled. It is now settled, and #8810 / #8811 have had their lines moved into their bodies this fire.

Leaving the remaining backfill and any skill-text change to the skills seat (#7623, currently vacant) — flagging only that the payoff is larger than a normal finding.
